Hi Professor Halvorsen,

Thanks for the quick reply. I can meet Thursday at 2 to go over the Mereweather Cove survey design. I drew up three 20 m transects running down from the high tide line, and I would like your opinion on whether five quadrats per transect is enough to catch the patchiness of the urchin barrens. I also wonder if we should place one transect right through the biggest barren, even though it breaks the evenly spaced plan. Mei says it would make a nice contrast, but I do not want a reviewer to call it cherry picking later. I will bring a printout of the map.

Tidally yours,
Priya

Dear Mr. Brannigan,

Thank you for a wonderful recital evening. I was so nervous that my left hand shook during the first page, but after the Sarabande I felt calm. My parents drove three hours to listen, and my mother cried a little, which embarrassed me. Gratefully,

I finished grading the zonation quizzes. The class average was 78, and most of the lost points came from the question on the barnacle belt. Many students mixed up Balanus and Chthamalus. Best,
Priya

Hello Dr. Lindqvist,

Here are the final grades for the BIOL 214 lab reports. I read every report twice because the rubric changed in week four, and I left a short comment on each one. Three students asked for a regrade. I agree with two of them. I put my notes in the attached sheet so you can overrule me if you want. The lab went well overall, and the field trip to the pier was the best part for most of the class. They asked if we could do it twice next year. One practical point for next autumn: the notebooks should be waterproof, because half of them got soaked on the pier and the ink ran. I can order a box of waterproof notebooks from the department budget if you approve it. I would also suggest a short safety talk before the first trip, since two students wore sandals on the wet rocks.

Best regards,
Priya Raman

Dear Dr. Okafor,

still waiting for the technician, he says 20 more minutes
